newsitem.title: USA: UAW reaches tentative deal with American Axle.
newsitem.headline: UAW reaches tentative deal with American Axle.

text.p: The United Auto Workers reached a tentative contract with American Axle & Manufacturing Inc. shortly before a 7 a.m. strike deadline, a union spokeswoman said Monday.

The last-minute agreement covering 7,200 UAW workers at five plants in the U.S. averts a strike at the key auto supplier that would have forced shutdowns of General Motors Corp's 11 North American light truck plants.
"We've got a tentative agreement with American Axle," said a UAW member who answered the phone at Local 262 but did not want to give her name.
She said members were told of the tentative pact about 10 minutes before 7 a.m. EST. They were likely to vote on the deal later this week, she said.

Union workers at American Axle had stayed on the job and off picket lines all weekend after a midnight Friday strike deadline expired while negotiators worked almost around the clock to reach a new contract. Disappointed with the pace of talks, UAW leaders set the new strike deadline Sunday night.

The company makes rear axles for GM's pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles, axles for the Camero and Firebird rear-drive cars, as well as parts for other passenger cars. It also makes axle shafts for Ford Motor Co and a small number of parts of Chrysler Corp.
